articles.summary: Last week’s security disclosures offered a glimpse of the challenges ahead. Critical flaws surfaced across software that much of the internet depends on. AI agents are making vulnerabilities faster and easier to find, while the time from discovery to exploitation continues to shrink. Companies increasingly need agents both to defend against threats and to transform how work gets done. As agents take on more responsibility, security must scale with autonomy. Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, recently posed a question to every company adopting AI: “There are billions of dollars being spent on coding, is your coding harness secure?” For security leaders, his recommendation is clear: establish guardrails for agent deployments and deploy a second set of eyes to monitor them for drift, compliance, and verifiability. At Replit, we’ve spent years building security into the infrastructure where agents work. When these vulnerabilities surfaced last week, that very foundation enabled us to respond quickly, effectively, and at scale. Our existing isolation protections prevented exploitation of the disclosed kernel vulnerabilities. We went further, patching affected tooling and deploying firewall protections centrally, reducing the remediation work developers would otherwise have had to do themselves. We believe the next step is to automate more of the security response itself, with people defining the policies, approvals, and intervention points that govern the process.

articles.summary: Established Italian manufacturer adds approximately 185 personnel and three facilities as management focuses on customer programs, deliveries and cash generation DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) (“NUBURU” or the “Company”) today highlighted the completion of its acquisition of a 70% controlling interest in TEKNE S.p.A. (“TEKNE”), its previously reported stockholders’ equity position, and its operating priorities as the Company’s NYSE American equity compliance plan period approaches its October 29, 2026 deadline. The completed TEKNE acquisition advances NUBURU’s transformation into an integrated defense and security technology business. TEKNE brings an established Italian defense manufacturer with approximately 185 personnel across three facilities in Ortona, Poggiofiorito and Guastalla, capabilities spanning specialized vehicles, defense mobility and electronic warfare. The Company’s October 22, 2026 commercial update reported categories totaling approximately $96.8 million of remaining order and program value in TEKNE’s September operating schedule. This preliminary, unaudited measure covers 100% of TEKNE and includes conditional items; it is not validated signed backlog, recognized revenue or a revenue forecast. Realization depends on program activation where required, production funding, delivery, customer acceptance and collection. With the transaction closed, management’s focus is on integration, execution and measurable financial results. TEKNE Acquisition Expands NUBURU’s Industrial Foundation NUBURU’s 70% controlling interest in TEKNE extends the Company’s operating presence beyond its historical laser technology business into established industrial manufacturing serving defense and security customers. TEKNE’s facilities, workforce and specialized technologies provide the industrial base for NUBURU’s integrated defense and security strategy, and create opportunities to coordinate TEKNE’s manufacturing expertise with NUBURU’s laser technologies and complementary software capabilities. Financial Position and NYSE American Compliance As of June 30, 2026, NUBURU reported stockholders’ equity of approximately $10.13 million, above the $4.0 million stockholders’ equity threshold identified in its prior NYSE American compliance disclosures. This marked the Company’s second consecutive quarter of positive stockholders’ equity, following a stockholders’ deficit of approximately $15.18 million at December 31, 2025. The Company’s compliance plan period under its NYSE American continued listing standards concludes on October 29, 2026. Any determination regarding the Company’s compliance status rests with NYSE American, and NUBURU will communicate material developments regarding its listing status through its established public disclosure channels. From Orders to Deliveries, Revenue and Cash With TEKNE in the group, NUBURU is placing increased emphasis on converting its industrial capabilities and signed order book into measurable business performance. The Company’s operational priorities are: Order execution: advancing customer orders through manufacturing and fulfillment. Deliveries: completing and delivering products and systems on schedule. Revenue realization: translating completed commercial activity into recognized revenue. Cash collections: driving working capital, customer payments and cash generation. Financial discipline: aligning operating expenditures and capital allocation with business priorities. The objective is straightforward: convert orders into deliveries, deliveries into revenue, and revenue into cash — building the foundation for sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value. Completed Milestones and Near-Term Priorities Completed milestones Completed the acquisition of a 70% controlling interest in TEKNE S.p.A. on October 15, 2026. Expanded the industrial operating base through TEKNE’s established Italian manufacturing operations. Added capabilities in specialized vehicles, defense mobility and electronic warfare. Reported stockholders’ equity of approximately $10.13 million as of June 30, 2026, above the $4.0 million threshold identified in prior NYSE American compliance disclosures. Near-term priorities Advance integration of TEKNE’s manufacturing and operating capabilities. Prioritize conversion of orders into deliveries, recognized revenue and cash collections. Develop commercial opportunities across defense mobility, electronic warfare, laser technologies and complementary software. Maintain financial discipline and oversight of capital resources. Provide shareholders with measurable operational and financial updates, including on applicable listing requirements. Management Commentary Alessandro Zamboni, Executive Chairman and Co-CEO of NUBURU, commented: “NUBURU today is a fundamentally different company from the one that entered 2026. We have closed TEKNE, repaid approximately $16.75 million of principal under our December 2025 debenture and Lyocon acquisition notes, reported two consecutive quarters of positive stockholders’ equity and built an industrial platform with established customer programs. Our job now is execution — turning that platform into deliveries, revenue and cash — and we will keep shareholders informed on every material development, including our listing status, through our public disclosures.” Dario Barisoni, Co-CEO of NUBURU and CEO of NUBURU Defense LLC, added: “TEKNE provides the industrial foundation for connecting our defense mobility and electronic-warfare capabilities with laser technologies and operational-resilience software. Our focus is to develop integrated solutions around specific customer requirements, with clear responsibility for technical validation, delivery and support. We intend to build on equipment deliveries with software, maintenance and lifecycle services, creating more repeatable business across the platform.” Gianluca Trezza, Chief Executive Officer and General Manager of TEKNE S.p.A., said: “TEKNE brings established manufacturing capabilities, experienced personnel and specialized defense technologies to NUBURU’s industrial strategy. With the acquisition completed, our priority is execution — advancing manufacturing activities, fulfilling customer requirements and translating our industrial capabilities into measurable business results.” Transparency and Shareholder Accountability NUBURU believes shareholder confidence is earned through operating performance, financial transparency and consistent delivery against stated objectives. NUBURU will continue reporting material developments through its established public disclosure channels, with particular emphasis on operational milestones, financial performance, commercial progress and applicable listing requirements. About NUBURU Inc NUBURU, Inc. (NYSE American: BURU) is developing a dual-use Defense & Security platform combining electronic warfare and defense mobility, laser and photonics engineering, operational-resilience software and AI-assisted orchestration, and advanced manufacturing and support. Its strategy is to integrate operating businesses and developing technologies into solutions for defense, security, critical-infrastructure and industrial customers. NUBURU’s operating capabilities include Tekne’s special-vehicle and electronic-system engineering, Lyocon’s laser expertise and Orbit’s operational-resilience software. Integrated mission packages and technologies under development remain subject to validation and applicable approvals. For more information, visit www.nuburu.net . And with Microsoft IQ, we're making the rich enterprise context underneath Microsoft 365 + Foundry + Fabric available to agentic workloads. Nearly 60K customers are accessing context across Microsoft IQ, up 25% QoQ. Third, we’re also helping customers secure and govern their agents at scale. Over 50M agents are now in A365, up 30% QoQ. articles.summary: Precision Resource Breaks Ground on Two New Production Additive Manufacturing Facilities and Expands Value-Added Services in Partnership with 3D Systems Elizabeth Piet Wed, 10/28/2026 - 15:07 Release Date Wednesday, Oct 28, 2026 4:30 PM Precision Resource expands U.S. production metal additive manufacturing footprint with new locations in California and Connecticut Expands Precision Resource's additive manufacturing network and supports a more integrated manufacturing solution for commercial and defense customers Deploys 3D Systems' metal additive manufacturing technology to expand production capacity, accelerate production at scale, and support long-term growth ROCK HILL, South Carolina, and SHELTON, Conn. October 28, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE:DDD) and Precision Resource , a leader in the production of critical components for the automotive, heavy-duty, aerospace, and medical device industries, today announced the groundbreaking of two new additive manufacturing locations, one in Huntington Beach, California, and one in Shelton, Connecticut. Precision Resource will further add in-house heat treatment and expand its complex machining capabilities, giving commercial and defense customers a more integrated path from 3D printed part to finished component. The facilities will utilize advanced metal additive manufacturing systems from 3D Systems and are expected to be operational in Q1 2027, a milestone that coincides with Precision Resource's 80th year in business. In Huntington Beach, California, Precision Resource is breaking ground on its second additive manufacturing location. This expansion will double the site’s current industrial additive manufacturing capacity. In Shelton, Connecticut, the company is breaking ground on its first additive manufacturing location that can further expand as demand grows. Together, the Huntington Beach and Shelton investments expand Precision Resource's additive manufacturing ecosystem and strengthen its partnership with 3D Systems, creating a connected manufacturing network across both locations. The expansion positions Precision Resource to significantly increase production capacity while creating one of the most comprehensive metal additive manufacturing networks in North America, supporting growing demand from commercial and defense customers. "This expansion is much more than adding machines. We are building something significant by connecting our Huntington Beach and Shelton operations into an integrated additive manufacturing network," said Chris Gratton, Director of Additive and Machine Operations at Precision Resource. "Together, these operations give our customers greater capacity, flexibility, and a faster path from print to finished component. They also allow us to reduce supply-chain complexity, provide greater manufacturing and geographic redundancy, and take on increasingly demanding production programs with the speed, quality and reliability our customers require." Precision Resource is expanding its additive manufacturing capabilities with the addition of 3D Systems' DMP Flex 350 Triple metal 3D printing technology. These new machines add to the fleet of DMP 350 systems already in operation at Precision Resource, further expanding a proven additive manufacturing platform that has supported the company's growth in production applications across commercial and defense markets. The platform combines high-throughput production with exceptional part quality and repeatability, helping Precision Resource meet growing demand for complex, production-grade metal components across commercial and defense markets. "Precision Resource has established itself as a leader in delivering high-quality, production-ready metal components to demanding markets," said Reji Puthenveetil, EVP, Additive Solutions and Chief Commercial Officer, 3D Systems. "This expansion demonstrates how additive manufacturing is increasingly becoming an integrated production solution for critical commercial and defense applications. By combining Precision Resource's manufacturing expertise with 3D Systems' advanced DMP technology and application expertise, these new facilities will help accelerate the adoption of high-volume, production-grade metal additive manufacturing for critical commercial and defense applications while providing customers with the scale, consistency, and reliability required for mission-critical programs." About Precision Resource Founded in 1947, Precision Resource is a global manufacturer of custom engineered metal components headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut. The company serves automotive, heavy duty, medical, semiconductor, commercial and defense markets with capabilities including fine blanking, grinding, lapping, laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing, heat treatment and complex machining. Learn more at www.precisionresource.com About 3D Systems For 40 years, Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials, and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. articles.summary: Brings live supervision, quality scoring, journey analytics, and staffing forecasts so contact centers can manage AI and human agents together RingCX now available for mobile and in Microsoft Teams BELMONT, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- RingCentral, Inc. (NYSE: RNG), a global leader in AI-powered customer engagement, today announced new AI capabilities for RingCX Ⓡ that give contact centers one place to supervise, measure, and plan for AI and human agents as a single workforce. AI agents now handle a growing share of customer conversations, and contact center managers and supervisors need the same visibility and control over them that they have over people. RingCX now extends live supervision, quality scoring, journey analytics, and staffing forecasts to AI agents, including RingCentral AI Receptionist™ (AIR) and AIR Pro, so supervisors can monitor performance, evaluate interactions, understand customer journeys, and plan capacity from one dashboard. These capabilities are designed to help contact centers improve first contact resolution, reduce handle time, and lower customer service costs. “AI agents are becoming part of the everyday customer engagement workforce, and managing them alongside human agents presents a tremendous opportunity to improve contact center operations,” said Jim Dvorkin, SVP of Customer Experience Products at RingCentral. “With RingCX, leaders see every customer conversation in one place, whether an AI agent or a human agent is handling it. They can step in sooner, hold quality to one standard, and plan staffing for the whole workforce, so more customers get their issue resolved in one go, with no need to call back.” “Having AI and human agents work together is only valuable if we can see what's actually happening across the full journey between them,” said Tasha McIntosh, Senior Patient Care Manager, EVP Eyecare. “We’ve been finding that when a customer's request doesn't match what our AI agent expects, that gap can slip through until the patient calls back frustrated. With these new RingCX features, we’ll now have one system that can catch that kind of mismatch before it becomes a bad experience, instead of after.” Delivering Better Customer Outcomes with AI and Human Agents Working Together RingCentral’s new AI capabilities enable organizations to: Seamlessly transfer between AI and human agents in both directions while preserving context. Surface AI agent interactions in the same live view as human agents , so supervisors can catch issues and intervene in real time, regardless of whether the interaction is handled by an AI or human agent. Score every AI agent interaction against the same rubric used for human agents , providing quality and compliance leaders with one complete, sentiment-scored view of the customer regardless of who handled the conversation. Track the complete AI-to-human journey , providing consistent insights into the performance of AI agents and human agents. Forecast staffing needs across AI and human agent capacity together, so schedules reflect the whole workforce. “Bringing AI and human agents under common visibility will give businesses more confidence to begin or expand agentic AI,” said Sheila McGee-Smith, President & Principal Analyst, McGee-Smith Analytics. “The next challenge will be personal AI agents: as consumers increasingly use agents to act on their behalf, contact centers will need to recognize, route, and measure both inbound and outbound AI-agent traffic. Understanding the full AI-to-human customer journey will become essential.” Sample use cases include: Real-time monitoring and handoff: A member of a regional health plan calls about a denied claim. An AI agent answers initial questions and gathers details while a supervisor watches the conversation live. If human empathy is needed, the supervisor steps in and the conversation moves to a human agent with context intact, so the member gets clear next steps without repeating their story. Seasonal staffing: A retail workforce planner schedules AI agents into the holiday seasonal staffing forecast. AI agents handle routine shipping and return questions overnight and on weekends, while human agents handle escalations, covering peak-seasonal surge without the cost of temporary hires. Escalation rate tracking: A quality leader at a regional bank sees fraud dispute calls handled by AI agents have the highest escalation rate of any intent. The team routes those calls straight to human agents, and fraud customers reach a human agent at first attempt, improving first contact resolution. AI Onboarding, Wherever Agents Work In addition to managing AI and human agents, RingCentral is introducing AI Onboarding for RingCX, designed to simplify and accelerate contact center setup, and shorten the configuration work that delays go-live. Administrators can describe their desired configuration in natural language. RingCentral AI builds the configuration plan, executes it through RingCX APIs, and validates routing with a simulated test before go-live. RingCX Available for Mobile, Microsoft Teams RingCX is available for mobile, enabling call center agents to receive and handle routed RingCX voice calls from their mobile phones using the RingCentral mobile app, helping reduce missed calls. Additionally, RingCX in Microsoft Teams brings contact center capabilities directly into Microsoft Teams, allowing organizations to manage customer interactions within an interface employees already use, without adding another vendor. Availability These new AI capabilities are being showcased at ICMI 2026 in Orlando, Florida, on October 28-29; booth #505. For additional details or demo requests, visit or click here . Powered by advanced AI, RingCentral delivers intelligence across the conversation journey—before, during, and after every human interaction. articles.summary: The Short Version Firms with automated receivables average about 40 days sales outstanding (DSO). Firms without automation average 47. That gap is roughly a week of cash. In PYMNTS survey data, 87% of firms with automated AR reported faster overall processes, and 75% reported better customer experience. Inaccurate payment matching sends collectors after customers who have already paid. Recurring-billing clients notice this quickly, because they hear from you every cycle. Manual remittance handling breaks in three recurring ways: retyping errors, payments that arrive without remittance details, and incorrect matches that leave paid invoices open. The World Bank’s 6.49% average remittance cost measures person-to-person transfers. It gives you no reliable basis for estimating B2B receivables costs. Should you automate accounts receivable? In short: yes, if you bill on a recurring cycle or your team sends more invoices than it can track by hand. Teams that automate report faster processes, lower DSO, and fewer errors. If you send a handful of simple invoices a month, manual work may still hold up.

articles.summary: The Short Version A controlled CSV sync into Dynamics 365 beats keying payments by hand, as long as someone owns reconciliation after the file posts. Here are the key points: Reconciling bank statements against the AR ledger after each import is recurring work that often gets skipped. When it does, errors stay hidden until month-end. If the record count or the control total (the sum of the Amount column) doesn’t match, stop the import before any payments post. A date written as 03/04 means March or April depending on locale, and it can land in the wrong period without anyone noticing. Spreadsheets strip leading zeros from customer IDs like 00412. A decimal-separator mismatch between 1.250,00 and 1,250.00 changes the imported amount. One transfer covering three subscription invoices, with only a contract number on the remittance, leaves your team tracing three separate Dynamics 365 invoice IDs. When a CSV sync is worth it, and when to keep typing Use a structured file workflow if payment volume makes retyping costly. Don’t expect it to clean up bad source data. The weak point comes after import, when the file posts and nobody owns reconciliation.
